title: Sell Mineral Rights in Despard, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Despard, WV | Harrison County
metaDescription: Despard, WV mineral owner just outside Clarksburg? We buy Harrison County fractional interests and old leases directly, title-checked before any offer.
heroLead: Despard sits just outside Clarksburg in Harrison County, close enough to the county seat that its mineral history runs on the same track as the city's, without the same volume of courthouse paper to sort through.
intro: Small unincorporated communities like Despard often get treated as an afterthought in county-wide leasing summaries, but the mineral tracts here are subject to the same Harrison County lease and unit activity as anywhere else in the county, and the same layered coal-and-gas history that produced separate estates on a single parcel.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Despard directly, confirming exactly what your family holds before naming a figure.

sections.heading: Close to Clarksburg, same leasing pressure
paragraphs: Operators working Harrison County don't stop leasing at the Clarksburg city line. Despard-area tracts have seen the same Marcellus and Utica interest as the rest of the county, and a family here may find their acreage already inside an active unit.

sections.heading: Older leases still on the books
paragraphs: As with much of Harrison County, some Despard-area leases predate the statutory conversion requiring flat-rate leases to pay a minimum one-eighth royalty. We check whether your family's lease qualifies before pricing the interest.

sections.heading: Small tracts, real fractional interests
paragraphs: Interests around Despard tend to be smaller and more fractional than in Clarksburg itself, often the remainder of a farm tract split among heirs decades ago. We trace the deed and probate record to confirm your exact percentage.

It's not unusual for a Despard-area family to hold an interest that was never separately deeded out on its own, just carried along inside a larger conveyance decades ago, which is another reason we verify the recorded description before naming a number.

faqs.question: Is my Despard-area tract inside an active drilling unit?
faqs.answer: It's possible. We check current unit orders and lease records for Harrison County covering your specific tract.

faqs.question: How do I know if my family's lease is a flat-rate lease?
faqs.answer: The recorded lease will specify either a fixed dollar amount per well or a royalty percentage. We review the actual instrument to confirm which applies to you.

faqs.question: My interest is a small fraction of a larger tract. Is it still worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Often yes. We regularly buy small fractional shares once the exact percentage is confirmed from the recorded chain of title.

faqs.question: What if my interest was never separately deeded to me by name?
faqs.answer: That's common where an interest passed inside a larger family conveyance. We trace it through the underlying deed and any probate records to confirm your share.
